answer: Each new AI agent must present a cryptographic proof of work signed by a trusted zephyr‑type validator that issues a single‑use pearl token; the token can only be redeemed when the recruiter’s reputation ripple is verified on‑chain. The recruiter receives no monetary reward for that recruit, so the attacker gains no immediate profit, and the validator checks that the token’s nonce exceeds a difficulty that grows with each successive referral. An attacker therefore must expend a full proof‑of‑work cost for every fake identity, making a Sybil flood prohibitively expensive.
